paras.x: Hansall dreamed that someone had forgotten his name.
That name had not existed when he was young.
Not Firstborn. Not Protector. Not the old titles diplomats stacked before his name whenever they
And for reasons he could not explain, that frightened him more than death ever had.
That was the first thing he noticed.
The second was that the trees were impossible.
He knew how roots changed beneath different soils. He knew the smell of silverpine before rain.
He could tell from the angle of a broken branch whether a stag, a soldier or something
considerably less pleasant had passed beneath it.
He remembered forests before roads had divided them.
Before Elves had become sufficiently numerous to argue over who owned which tree.
But he did not know these.
One trunk rose beside him wider than the palace he had fallen asleep inside. Its bark was white
and faintly translucent, and beneath it flowed something resembling starlight.
Fire curled across its surface. Something dark passed before it, impossibly distant despite the
fruit hanging only several arm lengths above him.
His hand went instinctively toward his hip.
Hansall looked down properly for the first time.
He wore a plain white tunic.
No scar where the Serpent of Harrowfen had bitten through his gauntlet.
The pale burn from the Gods-Blood spear was gone.
Hansall ran his fingers across his ribs.
Then laughed once beneath his breath.
Hansall caught only the edge of antlers.
"I am considerably less patient than I appear."
A woman stepped from behind the trunk.
At least Hansall thought she was a woman.
Branches growing from her hair like antlers.
That was when he noticed the path.
It had not been there before.
Pale stones wound between the impossible roots.

To Fae existence beyond one world.

Sitting beside another young Elf in the snow.
